habitat: Demoiselle cranes have one of the most spectacular migration routes of any crane, breeding in the grasslands, steppes, and semi-deserts of Central Asia from the Black Sea to Mongolia, and wintering in the Indian subcontinent and northeastern Africa. They are the smallest crane species, and unlike most cranes, they are adapted to dry, open landscapes — breeding in steppe grasslands, agricultural fields, and semi-arid regions far from water. They roost in shallow wetlands, riverbanks, and flooded fields.
diet: Demoiselle cranes are opportunistic omnivores, feeding on seeds, grains, grass shoots, tubers, insects (especially grasshoppers and beetles), lizards, and small mammals. During migration and wintering, they rely heavily on agricultural grains — wheat, rice, chickpeas, and millet — in fields across India and Pakistan. They forage primarily on the ground, walking and pecking.
behavior: Demoiselle cranes are exceptional migrators — they cross the Himalayas twice annually, flying at altitudes exceeding 7,000 meters through mountain passes, one of the most arduous migrations of any bird. They gather in enormous flocks of thousands during migration. Their courtship dances are elegant and balletic, involving bows, leaps, wing-spreads, and coordinated duets between mated pairs. Pairs mate for life. The species name 'demoiselle' means 'young lady' in French, referring to their delicate, graceful appearance.
facts: Demoiselle cranes are the smallest crane species at 85-100 cm tall with a 155-180 cm wingspan. Their most distinctive features are the long white feather tufts behind each eye and the elegant black 'waistcoat' of feathers draping over their chest. In India, they are known as 'koonj' and their arrival signals the changing seasons. In parts of Rajasthan, local communities traditionally feed migrating demoiselle cranes — a unique cultural practice. They can live 25-30 years.
naming: Demoiselle names might reflect their delicate beauty, extraordinary migration, or Central Asian origin. Consider names like Grace, Dancer, Ballerina, Himalayan, Koonj, Steppe, Mongolia, Skye, Feather, Breeze, or Aria.
